topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the core learning objectives of the lecture.

topics.label: Cancer etiology, intrinsic mutations, and epidemiological variation
topics.groupedBecause: They explore the fundamental interplay between intrinsic genetic mutations, environmental exposures, and global epidemiological patterns in cancer risk.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: They examine how infectious pathogens and associated immune disruption contribute to oncogenesis, illustrated by Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical and physical mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how chemical agents and physical radiation cause DNA damage directly, through reactive oxidative stress, or via metabolic activation.

topics.label: Tumour promotion and host susceptibility factors
topics.groupedBecause: They explain the mechanisms of non-mutagenic tumour promotion and how host developmental stages influence susceptibility to carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Methods for identifying and assessing carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: They detail the mutational signature, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro approaches used to determine carcinogenicity and evaluate human risk.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: It summarises the main conclusions of the lecture and closes the presentation.
